meta.description: Teach your child to recognise shame manipulation and reject labels others try to put on them. Game-based course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: "Nobody likes a greedy kid!" — and your child gives up who they are just to be accepted?
hero.subheadline: They share not because they want to. But because they're afraid of being labelled. This isn't about generosity — it's shame manipulation.

media.alt: A child pressured into giving up their things under threat of a label

pain.title: "Greedy" is a label used to make children act against themselves
pain.body:
At school, among friends, during break — someone says "nobody likes a greedy kid" and your child is already reaching for their things. Not because they want to share. But because they're afraid of being called greedy.

This isn't about generosity or learning to share. It's manipulation through shame: a label is attached to the child and they're pushed to act in order to avoid it. Without the skill to recognise this pattern, they give in automatically — even at their own expense.

The result — their boundaries gradually disappear, and others learn that one word is enough to make them back down. The child feels resentment but doesn't understand why — after all, they're "not greedy".

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
